title: Manual Xero Sync — recover or link a single record
content:
Manual Xero Sync — recover or link a single record

A self-service tool you can use whenever a single PayTrade ↔ Xero record needs to be re-pulled, re-pushed, or linked together. This guide walks through where the tool lives, who can use it, what each option does, and what to expect afterwards. For ongoing scheduled syncing you do not need this dialog — only reach for it when one specific record is out of step.

Where to find it and who can use it

The Manual sync button lives on the Xero Dashboard:

  1. Go to Integrations → Xero from the left sidebar.
  2. Open the Sync Log tab.
  3. Click the Manual sync button in the header (next to Refresh).

The dialog is available to Standard Users, Admins and Primary Admins on the company that owns the Xero connection. There is no separate permission to grant — if you can already view the Xero Dashboard, you can use Manual sync.

What the dialog looks like

Manual sync opens as a full-screen popup (about 95% of your browser window in each direction) so the side-by-side PayTrade and Xero panels have room to breathe. The popup uses the same surface colour as the rest of PayTrade and respects light / dark mode.

  • A Single record / Catch-up by date range tab switcher is pinned at the top — it stays visible while you scroll the body of the dialog.
  • The dialog header (with the close button) and footer (with Cancel, Check, and Run sync) are also fixed in place — only the middle section scrolls.
  • If you need even more room, the chevron pills on the inner edge of the left sidebar and the right AI panel let you collapse either rail without leaving the dialog.
  • Closing the dialog (Cancel, the X, or pressing Esc) discards any unticked review state — the next time you open Manual sync the form is fresh.

When should you use it?

Manual sync is the right tool for one record at a time. The most common reasons to open it are:

  • A missed sync — a record was created or paid in one system but never reached the other (for example a Xero webhook was missed, or a PayTrade payment was confirmed while Xero was disconnected).
  • A broken mapping — both records exist but PayTrade doesn't know they're the same one. This happens when an integration is reset, a contact is duplicated, or an invoice number is changed.
  • Linking two records that already exist on both sides — typically a contact created independently in PayTrade and in Xero that you now want to treat as one.

For everything else (a one-off blip, a transient API error, a slow webhook) it is usually safer to wait — the scheduled fallback sync runs automatically and will pick up missed events on its own.

The five record types you can sync

The first thing the dialog asks is which record type you want to sync. Pick the one that matches the thing that is missing or out of date:

Record typeUse it when…
Invoice / BillA payment claim is missing in Xero, an invoice/bill in Xero is missing in PayTrade, or the totals between the two sides have drifted.
PaymentA confirmed PayTrade payment leg never reached Xero, or a Xero payment is not showing on the PayTrade claim.
Bank Transfer (PT-RET retention)A cash-retention bank transfer (with a PT-RET-<payment id> reference) is missing or duplicated in Xero. There is no PayTrade-side picker for this — pick the linked payment instead.
ContactA client / supplier exists on both sides but isn't linked, or a Xero contact change isn't reflecting in PayTrade.
Manual Journal (retention gross-up)A retention gross-up journal in Xero needs to be re-imported. There is no PayTrade-side picker — these are produced automatically when retention is recorded.

The three things you can do with the dialog

The same dialog handles three workflows. You don't have to tell PayTrade which one you want — it works it out from what you fill in and what the pre-flight check finds.

A. Fix a missed sync — Xero → PayTrade (import)

Use this when the record exists in Xero but is missing or out of date in PayTrade.

  1. Pick the record type.
  2. Paste the Xero ID (or invoice/bill number for invoices and bills) into the Xero side picker.
  3. Leave the PayTrade side picker empty.
  4. Click Check, review the panel, tick I've reviewed this, then click Run sync.

PayTrade re-pulls the single record from Xero and runs it through the same handler used for live Xero webhook events — so retentions, smart-contract resolution, contact mapping, account/tax codes, tracking categories and audit-pack PDFs all run as normal.

B. Push a missing record — PayTrade → Xero

Use this when the record exists in PayTrade but never reached Xero (for example a confirmed payment leg).

  1. Pick the record type.
  2. Use the PayTrade side search box to find the record by id, amount, reference, contact name, project name or contract name.
  3. Leave the Xero side empty.
  4. Click Check, review the panel, tick I've reviewed this, then click Run sync.

PayTrade calls the same services used by the live confirm flows, so your Xero account codes, tax codes, tracking categories, retention recording mode and retention gross-up journals all apply automatically.

Note: Pushing a fully-paid Xero invoice from a PayTrade-only claim is blocked at pre-flight. Paid invoices in Xero must be imported instead — never overwritten.

C. Link two records that already exist on both sides

Use this when both records exist (in PayTrade and in Xero) but PayTrade doesn't know they're the same one.

  1. Pick the record type.
  2. Paste the Xero ID into the Xero-side picker.
  3. Also select the matching record from the PayTrade-side picker.
  4. Click Check — if the totals agree (within 1 cent), the recommended action will be link, which creates the mapping without overwriting either side. If totals disagree it falls back to import; if both sides are fully paid and totals disagree, the action is blocked.
  5. Tick I've reviewed this and click Run sync.

Where to find the IDs the dialog asks for

Record typePayTrade IDXero ID
Invoice / BillThe claim id at the top of the payment-claim page (/user/payment-claims/<id>) and the leading number in any Sync Log row's Reference column. The picker also accepts amount, claim reference, contact / business name, project name or contract name.Either the Invoice GUID (found in the Xero URL …Edit.aspx?InvoiceID=<GUID>) or the human-readable Invoice / Bill number (e.g. INV-0042). Both work.
PaymentThe payment id on the Payments page row, in the URL /user/payments/<id>, and on its Sync Log rows. The picker also accepts amount, memo or contact name.The Payment GUID from the Xero invoice's Payments tab — open the payment, the URL contains bankTransactionID=<GUID>.
Bank Transfer (PT-RET)Not selectable directly — pick the linked payment instead.The BankTransfer GUID from the Xero bank transfer screen, or the PT-RET-<payment id> reference shown on the transaction.
ContactThe client / supplier id on the Clients & Suppliers page row and in the URL /user/clients-suppliers/<id>. The picker also accepts contact or business name.The Contact GUID from the Xero contact URL https://go.xero.com/Contacts/View/<GUID>.
Manual JournalNot selectable — these are produced automatically by the retention gross-up flow.The ManualJournal GUID from the Xero URL …Journal/View.aspx?journalID=<GUID>.

What the pre-flight panel shows you

Before Run sync is enabled, the dialog runs a read-only pre-flight and shows a panel of typed checks. Each check is marked OK, warning or fail. You will typically see:

  • Live Xero lookup — confirms the Xero record is reachable on your current connection.
  • Mapping — whether a PayTrade ↔ Xero link already exists, and to which PayTrade id.
  • Amount agreement — Xero total vs PayTrade total, with the dollar difference.
  • Payment status — Unpaid, Part payment / pay less, Full payment, or Overpaid (credit on file). The latter two are flagged so you have a chance to spot pay-less or credit-note situations before syncing.
  • Xero credit notes (contact) — up to 10 outstanding credit notes on the Xero contact, with remaining credit. Helps explain pay-less or overpayment cases.
  • Payment legs reconciled — a side-by-side table of Xero payment legs vs PayTrade payment legs, with badges showing what each direction will do (✓ matched, → push, → import, unconfirmed).
  • Retention shape — retention line presence, shared-codes flag, and the signed net-retained amount.
  • Contact / project / contract / bank-account mapping — for invoices and bills, confirms every linked entity already has a local mapping.

Below the checks the panel shows the recommended action (import, push, link or blocked) and a one-line summary explaining why. You only need to tick I've reviewed this when you are happy with what you see — the same checkbox is enforced on the server, so it is not just a UI nudge.

What to expect after Run sync

The result panel appears below the form (the dialog does not close, so you can run another id straight after). It shows:

  • The direction that ran (import, push, link or blocked).
  • A plain-language message, e.g. "Invoice INV-0042 imported from Xero, mapped to claim 18327".
  • A clickable link to the matching Sync Log row, where you can see every check that ran and the full payload.

Each run writes one of three Sync Log rows:

  • Two-sided manual Xero sync triggered — the run succeeded.
  • Two-sided manual Xero sync was blocked by pre-flight — only used when the recommended action is blocked (for example, both sides fully paid but totals disagree).
  • Two-sided manual Xero sync failed during dispatch — the run was attempted but the underlying service reported an error.

For backwards compatibility every run also emits a legacy Manual Xero sync triggered row, so existing Sync Log filters by that label continue to surface manual runs.

Troubleshooting & FAQ

The pre-flight failed with "Live Xero lookup". Your Xero connection may have expired. Reconnect Xero from Integrations → Xero and try again.

The action is showing as blocked and Run sync is disabled. The dialog blocks runs that would overwrite paid records when totals don't agree. Open the underlying records in PayTrade and Xero, fix the difference (typically a credit note or pay-less amount), then re-Check.

I pasted an invoice number but Xero says "not found". Check that the number matches exactly — including any prefix and leading zeros. If the invoice was renumbered in Xero, paste the GUID instead.

Xero rejects the link with a duplicate-contact or duplicate-invoice error. The two records can't be merged automatically. Pick one as the source of truth, archive the other, and re-run Manual sync against the surviving id.

I got a warning about "unconfirmed" PayTrade legs. A leg exists in PayTrade but hasn't been confirmed yet. Confirm the payment in PayTrade first, then re-run Manual sync — the dialog will then push it through.

Should I use Manual sync, or wait for the scheduled sync? If the issue is a one-off (a transient API error, a momentarily-down connection) the scheduled fallback usually picks it up within an hour. Use Manual sync when the record has been stuck for longer than that, when you need it fixed before a deadline, or when you can see the two sides have drifted permanently.

Next steps

  • Open Integrations → Xero → Sync Log and try a no-op Check on a record you know is healthy — this is a safe way to learn the dialog without changing anything.
  • If you regularly need Manual sync for the same record, please contact support — repeated manual syncs usually point to an underlying configuration issue (a missing account code, a duplicate contact, or a lost mapping) we can help you fix permanently.

title: Manual Xero Sync — catch-up discovery by date range
content:
Manual Xero Sync — catch-up discovery by date range

Use the catch-up tab when you don't already know a single record id but suspect drift between PayTrade and Xero across a window of time — for example after a long Xero outage, after restoring from a backup, or before an end-of-month review. The tab lists everything that touched the window on either side, classifies each row, lets you pick exactly the rows you want to fix, and then drives the standard per-record sync sequentially with full pre-flight, action-token, and per-row sync-log audit trail.

Where to find it

  1. Go to Integrations → Xero from the left sidebar.
  2. Open the Sync Log tab and click the Manual sync button.
  3. At the top of the dialog switch from Single record to Catch-up by date range.

The tab opens with a last-30-days window pre-filled so you can hit Discover immediately. Both ends of the window are honoured — for contacts the upper bound is filtered client-side off Xero's UpdatedDateUTC.

What the catch-up tab looks like

The catch-up tab shares the same full-screen popup as the single-record tab (about 95% of your browser window in each direction). The wider canvas was added specifically for this tab — the side-by-side PayTrade and Xero results table genuinely needs the room.

  • The Single record / Catch-up by date range tab switcher stays pinned at the top of the dialog while you scroll through results.
  • Directly under the tab switcher sits the filter row — record type, From date, To date, and the Discover button — so you can re-narrow the window without scrolling back up.
  • Each result row has a checkbox on the left and an Actions column on the right (with the sync log link that appears once a row has been processed). Rows that are already in sync or blocked can't be ticked — only actionable rows accept selection.
  • The selection state is driven by the parent dialog, so what you see ticked in the table is exactly what the Run sync on N selected button at the bottom will operate on. Toggle a row off and the count updates immediately.
  • If a wide window or wide contact / project names crowd the table, collapse the left sidebar and / or the right AI panel using the chevron pills on their inner edges to reclaim the screen width.
  • Clicking a row opens a per-record detail view in the same full-screen frame; the Back to results control returns you to the table with your selections intact.

What discovery looks at

Discovery is read-only — clicking Discover never changes data on either side. Three record types are supported:

  • Invoices / Bills — PayTrade payment claims (in scope: claims that have both a project and a contract, since those are the rows that flow to Xero with tracking categories) compared against Xero invoices whose line-item tracking resolves to a known PayTrade project.
  • Payments — PayTrade payment rows compared against Xero payment rows in window.
  • Contacts — PayTrade client/supplier rows compared against Xero contacts modified in window.

Each side is capped at 200 rows per discovery. If either side hits the cap a Truncated — narrow your window warning appears and you should pick a smaller date range.

Reading the results table

Results are shown as a true side-by-side two-column table: the PayTrade record on the left, the Xero record on the right, and a colour-coded status pill in the middle. Where only one side exists, the other column is greyed out with a no row in window placeholder so you can see at a glance whether you're chasing a missed push or a missed import.

PillMeaningSelectable?
LinkedBoth sides exist, mapping row exists, totals agree.No — nothing to do.
Needs linkBoth sides exist independently and pair on invoice number or contract+amount±$0.01+date±2 days, but no mapping row yet.Yes — pre-flight will recommend Link.
Amounts disagreeSides are linked or paired but totals differ by more than $0.01. Re-importing from Xero will overwrite the PayTrade row.Yes — pre-flight will pick the canonical direction.
PT only — needs pushPayTrade has the record, Xero side has nothing matching in window.Yes — pre-flight will recommend Push.
Xero only — needs importXero has the record, PayTrade side has nothing matching in window.Yes — pre-flight will recommend Import.
BlockedPre-flight precondition known to fail (for example PayTrade claim already locally paid so push is blocked).No — fix the precondition first.

Running the batch

  1. Tick the rows you want to act on. Linked and Blocked rows can't be ticked.
  2. Tick the I've reviewed these N records checkbox. This is the same per-row review gate as the single-record flow — without it the dispatcher refuses to run.
  3. Click Run sync on N selected. The batch runs sequentially with a small delay between rows so we don't hammer Xero. Each row independently calls pre-flight, then the same audited two-sided sync the single-record tab uses, then writes its own sync-log entry (template 518 / 519 / 520).
  4. The progress badge shows Running 3 / 12 and per-row pass/fail badges with a sync-log id link. If one row fails the batch keeps going to the next — partial success is the expected outcome of a recovery tool.

What it deliberately does not do

  • No bank-transfer or manual-journal discovery — those records are produced by confirming a payment / posting a gross-up journal, not recovered ad-hoc here.
  • No contact creation in Xero from this dialog — contact pushes are owned by the contact-sync settings.
  • No background queue — closing the dialog cancels remaining rows.
  • No new sync engine — every row goes through the same code path as the single-record tab so the audit trail is identical.
